title: bug: PowerShell daemon autostart splits project paths containing spaces in Start-Process ArgumentList
description: Native PS5.1 and pwsh7 probe reproduces Start-Process -ArgumentList @($daemonScript,"start","--project",$projectPath) splitting control é [x] $;' into four argv elements; --project receives only ...\control. The new literal-project-path real-wrapper claude cases time out with Daemon failed to start within 10s after the wildcard fix. Existing comment incorrectly says Start-Process re-quotes each array element; approved task-3ad573a7 scope forbids changing native argv.
definitionOfDone: Preserve complete daemon-script and project paths as individual native arguments on PS5.1 and pwsh7, including spaces and the literal fixture name.
Regression test fails with current ArgumentList construction and passes with the fix.
Keep daemon start error handling and escaped current FileSystem working directory unchanged.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (RED before the fix). Create scripts/tests/daemon-autostart-argv.test.mjs (node:test, ESM, LF, no BOM) with the Write tool and add its CI step with the Edit tool (ci.yml may be CONTESTED with task-3ad573a7 at landing; only a TOOL witness lands it). Reuse the engine detection and killTree shape of scripts/tests/protected-agent-command.test.mjs and the fake-daemon ppid trick of postflight.ps1's [protected runtime] P6 row.

Header comment: Start-Process -ArgumentList (PowerShell 5.1 and 7) joins its entries with single spaces and quotes none of them, so moe-agent.ps1's daemon autostart split the project "control é [x] $;'" into --project <root>\control, é, [x], $;' and the launcher timed out with 'Daemon failed to start within 10s' (task-8c875cc8).

Engines (win32 only): PowerShell 5.1 = path.join(SystemRoot, 'System32', 'WindowsPowerShell', 'v1.0', 'powershell.exe'); PowerShell 7 = the absolute path `where.exe pwsh.exe` prints, resolved with the parent env because the rows run with a scrubbed PATH. Skip reasons: off win32 'Start-Process builds a native Windows command line; run this file with Windows node (node.exe from WSL)'; pwsh missing 'pwsh.exe not found'.

Per test: root = fs.realpathSync.native(fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'moe-autostart-'))) (native realpath expands 8.3 names such as RUNNER~1, so argv compares exactly); t.after removes it (rmSync recursive, force, maxRetries 5, retryDelay 200). LITERAL = "control é [x] $;'". The fake daemon, written as fake-daemon.cjs into a given dir:
  const fs = require('fs'), path = require('path');
  fs.writeFileSync(process.env.FAKE_DAEMON_RECORD, JSON.stringify(process.argv.slice(1)));
  const project = process.argv[process.argv.indexOf('--project') + 1];
  // process.ppid is the launcher, which outlives the start poll that probes this pid.
  if (project && fs.existsSync(path.join(project, '.moe'))) fs.writeFileSync(path.join(project, '.moe', 'daemon.json'), JSON.stringify({ pid: process.ppid, port: 1, projectPath: project }));
Child env: process.env minus keys matching /^(MOE_|FAKE_|CLAUDE|CODEX|GEMINI|GROK|XAI|GIT_)/i and PSModulePath (an inherited 5.1/7 module path breaks the other engine); exactly one PATH key (find it case-insensitively; Windows calls it Path) = [dirname(process.execPath), System32, SystemRoot] joined by ';', so `Start-Process -FilePath "node"` resolves and no real agent CLI or git is reachable; HOME and USERPROFILE = path.join(root, 'home'); TEMP and TMP = path.join(root, 'tmp').

Row A, per engine: '<engine>: the daemon-autostart Start-Process passes literal-name paths as whole arguments'. Node writes cases.json (UTF-8) and a BOM'd driver.ps1 into root and runs <engine> -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File driver.ps1 -Wrapper <scripts/moe-agent.ps1> -Cases cases.json with cwd root; assert exit 0 with stderr in the message. The driver ($ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'): [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile the wrapper and throw on any parse error; take the CommandAst nodes whose GetCommandName() is 'Start-Process' and whose Extent.Text contains '--project' and throw unless exactly one; dot-source [scriptblock]::Create($f.Extent.Text) for every FunctionDefinitionAst whose Name is a command called inside that statement; then for each case ([IO.File]::ReadAllText | ConvertFrom-Json) set $env:FAKE_DAEMON_RECORD, $daemonScript and $projectPath and dot-source [scriptblock]::Create(<the statement's Extent.Text>). Cases: (1) script path.join(root, LITERAL, 'fake-daemon.cjs'), project path.join(root, LITERAL): the literal fixture name in BOTH arguments; (2) script path.join(root, 'plain', 'fake-daemon.cjs'), project path.join(root, 'a "b" c') + path.sep: spaces, double quotes and a trailing backslash (a drive root such as C:\ is a real project path). Create the script dirs, not the projects. Poll up to 20 s until every record exists, then assert each record deepEqual [script, 'start', '--project', project]; a missing record fails as 'node never ran the daemon script: its path was split'. Probed 2026-11-02 on 5.1.26100 and 7.6.9: the AST extract-and-run works on both, and today's construction gives [..., '--project', '<root>\control', 'é', '[x]', "$;'"].

Row B, per engine: '<engine>: the launcher autostarts the daemon under spaced project and daemon-script paths'. project = path.join(root, "control é $;'"), the literal fixture name without [x], because the target's path cmdlets read brackets as wildcards until task-3ad573a7 lands; write path.join(project, '.moe', 'project.json') = {"id":"proj-argv","name":"argv","settings":{"autoCommit":false}}. Daemon script = path.join(root, "daemon é $;' dir", 'fake-daemon.cjs'). Extra env: MOE_DAEMON_PATH = that script; MOE_PROXY_PATH = an inert path.join(root, 'proxy-stub.cjs') holding only a comment; MOE_DISABLE_HEARTBEAT=1; MOE_ACCOUNT_ROTATION=off; MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_ALLOW_WORKTREE_WRAPPER=1 (the suite may run from a task worktree; task-86431c31); FAKE_DAEMON_RECORD = path.join(root, 'wrapper-argv.json'). spawn(<engine>, ['-NoProfile', '-NonInteractive', '-ExecutionPolicy', 'Bypass', '-File', <scripts/moe-agent.ps1>, '-Project', project, '-WorkerId', 'worker-autostart-argv', '-Role', 'worker', '-NoLoop'], { cwd: root, env, windowsHide: true }). Stop it with taskkill /pid <child.pid> /T /F (that recorded PID only, never a pattern kill) as soon as stdout+stderr shows 'Daemon started (waited' or 'Daemon failed to start within', or at a 90 s cap. Assert the output matches /Daemon started \(waited/ and not /Daemon failed to start/, and the record deepEqual [script, 'start', '--project', project]. RED today: node gets the truncated <root>\daemon as its script and the launcher gives up after 10 s.

Error handling in the test: every driver and launcher spawn has a cap and reports its exit code, stdout and stderr in the assertion message; a spawn error (engine missing) fails the row with that error, not a hang; a missing record names which argument was split; t.after removes root even when an assertion fails.

implementationPlan.description:
FIX scripts/moe-agent.ps1 with the Edit tool (keep the UTF-8 BOM and LF endings; the path may be CONTESTED with task-3ad573a7 at landing, and only a TOOL witness lands it).
(a) Insert this block after `$script:GrokEnvPrev = $null` and its blank line, before the `# daemon.json is repository content:` comment, i.e. outside daemon-json-cap.test.mjs's helper segment, which starts at `function Read-MoeDaemonJsonText(`:
# Start-Process (PowerShell 5.1 and 7) joins -ArgumentList entries with single
# spaces and quotes none of them, so a path with a space reached node as several
# arguments. Quote every entry so the child's argv parser (the C runtime on
# Windows, .NET on Unix) splits the line back into the same entries.
function ConvertTo-MoeArgumentLine([string[]]$Arguments) {
    @($Arguments | ForEach-Object { '"' + ($_ -replace '(\\*)"', '$1$1\"' -replace '(\\+)$', '$1$1') + '"' }) -join ' '
}
Backslashes before a quote or at the end are doubled and a quote becomes backslash-quote. This exact body round-tripped, on 5.1.26100 and 7.6.9, the literal fixture name, an empty string, a "b" c\, x\\, a tab, q\"r and C:\. It calls no other wrapper function (row A defines only the functions the Start-Process statement itself calls).
(b) At the daemon autostart, replace the two comment lines `# Pass arguments as an array so paths containing spaces or quotes survive` and `# Windows command-line escaping (Start-Process re-quotes each element).` with own-line comments (no trailing comments: task-3ad573a7's scanner masks only full-line ones) saying Start-Process quotes nothing, so the launcher passes one pre-quoted command line, and change only the -ArgumentList argument:
        Start-Process -FilePath "node" -ArgumentList (ConvertTo-MoeArgumentLine @("$daemonScript", "start", "--project", "$projectPath")) -WindowStyle Hidden
Keep '--project' literally inside the statement (row A finds the call by it).
Error handling: the daemon start's error handling stays exactly as it is. A missing daemon script still ends with Write-Error 'Moe daemon script not found' and exit 1; a daemon that writes no live daemon.json within 10 s still ends with Write-Error 'Daemon failed to start within 10s' and exit 1; a Start-Process failure still terminates under $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'. Leave everything else as it is too: -FilePath "node", -WindowStyle Hidden, no -WorkingDirectory (task-3ad573a7 adds the escaped current FileSystem location on top of this change), and the MOE_DAEMON_PATH and global-install fallback with its Test-Path checks. moe-agent.sh already passes an argv array (DAEMON_ARGS), so there is no bash twin and no parity string to add.

completionSummary:

- moe-agent.ps1: new `ConvertTo-MoeArgumentLine` quotes each entry the way the C runtime parses it back: backslashes before a quote or at the end are doubled, and a quote becomes \". The autostart now passes `-ArgumentList (ConvertTo-MoeArgumentLine @("$daemonScript", "start", "--project", "$projectPath"))`. The wrong "re-quotes each element" comment is replaced. The helper sits above `function Read-MoeDaemonJsonText(`, so daemon-json-cap.test.mjs's segments are unchanged.
- Unchanged: -FilePath "node", -WindowStyle Hidden, no -WorkingDirectory (task-3ad573a7 adds it on top), the MOE_DAEMON_PATH and global-install fallback, both Write-Error exits and the 10 s wait loop. The UTF-8 BOM and LF endings are kept.

  - Row B runs the real launcher with a spaced project and a spaced MOE_DAEMON_PATH and expects "Daemon started (waited".
  - Each fake daemon records the exact argv node received.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: a Windows-only step "Test PowerShell daemon autostart arguments", placed after the daemon.json-cap step.
